page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-32 is a general-purpose server instance featuring 32 virtual CPUs and 124 GB of RAM. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor, the system allocates 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled on a dedicated basis. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1D cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores all placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. Multi-core performance is also strong, with Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU scores ranking in the top 10% and top 25% respectively. Cryptographic and vector instruction sets are supported, including AVX-512 and VAES, which contribute to strong performance in PassMark extended instructions and encryption tests. Memory bandwidth and database operations, such as Redis SET and PassMark database tests, perform in the average tier.

Given its balanced resource allocation of approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU and dedicated AMD EPYC processor, this instance delivers high compute density for general-purpose workloads. It is appropriate for software compilation, static web serving, and text or image processing pipelines. Additionally, it supports small-scale language model inference, demonstrating top-tier text generation speeds for 135M parameter models and average performance for 7B parameter models. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which should be factored into the overall resource architecture.
